changes.evidence: In X2, Stryker captures Xavier at Magneto's plastic prison and holds him at Alkali Lake, using Jason to make him run a copy of Cerebro, until the X-Men free him. The captor is named as Logan's record names Stryker's Alkali Lake operation (Weapon X).

In X-Men: Apocalypse, Apocalypse and his Horsemen kidnap Charles from the mansion and hold him in Cairo until the X-Men save him. At the end of Dark Phoenix he steps down as headmaster (Hank takes over) and moves to Paris, which is a retirement. Deadpool 2 (2018) then shows him in the mansion with the X-Men, so the X-Men stage comes back there. If the owner reads the Deadpool 2 cameo as non-canon, end the list at Independent from Dark Phoenix.

In X-Men Origins: Wolverine, Stryker tranquilizes teenage Scott and holds him at his Three Mile Island mutant prison for the Weapon XI program. Logan frees him, and Xavier collects the kids and takes them to his school. In X2, Stryker captures Scott at the plastic prison and brainwashes him at Alkali Lake until Jean frees him.

In Dark Phoenix, Jean knocks Scott out and leaves the mansion. She kills Raven at Red Hook, is banished from Genosha, and goes with Vuk against the X-Men. On the train she chooses to protect 'her family' again, before she vanishes into space.

This is the same Dark Phoenix move as A:fox-jean-grey-young. Jean leaves the mansion and is hunted by the X-Men and Magneto, then sides with her family again on the train. This file only uses Dark Phoenix, so every stage carries that title.
In X-Men (2000), Magneto's Brotherhood takes Rogue at the train station and holds her as the power source for his machine on Liberty Island, until Logan and the X-Men free her.

In X-Men: Apocalypse, Stryker captures Hank (with Raven, Moira and Peter) and holds him in a cell at Alkali Lake until Scott frees them. Hank then flies the X-Men to Cairo. The record's own step says he 'is captured by Stryker'.

In X-Men: Apocalypse, Stryker's men take Moira at the ruined mansion and lock her in a cell at Alkali Lake with Raven, Hank and Peter until Scott frees them. Afterwards, still with the CIA, she has Stryker arrested.

In X-Men: Apocalypse, after the mansion blast, Stryker's men capture Raven (with Hank, Moira and Peter) and hold her in a cell at the Alkali Lake (Weapon X) base until Scott blasts it open. She then leads the young mutants to Cairo and stays to train the X-Men. Before the capture she was only visiting Charles to find Erik, so the X-Men stage starts after the release.

In X-Men: Apocalypse, after the mansion blast, Stryker's men capture Raven (with Hank, Moira and Peter) and hold her in a cell at the Alkali Lake (Weapon X) base until Scott blasts it open. She then leads the young mutants to Cairo and stays to train the X-Men. Before the capture she was only visiting Charles to find Erik, so the X-Men stage starts after the release.

This record is on file only for The Wolverine and Days of Future Past. The Brotherhood stage dates from X-Men (2000), which is not one of its titles. By The Wolverine's post-credits scene, Magneto has his powers back and is working with Xavier to warn Logan, and in the dark 2023 he fights beside the X-Men. He holds no Brotherhood membership in any title on file.

In season 1, episode 10 ('Hostile'), Catherine and Geoffrey decide they no longer work for Jonah and leave PRIDE ('Leaving PRIDE'), skipping the next PRIDE meeting. In season 2, episode 1 ('Gimmie Shelter'), they rejoin the group to hunt the runaways ('Return to PRIDE').

owner_calls.question: In Dark Phoenix, the U.S. Mutant Containment Unit collars the X-Men and Erik's group and holds them on a train bound for a mutant internment facility, until the D'Bari attack. Should this in-title custody be a stage for everyone held? That is A:fox-cyclops-young, A:fox-charles-xavier-young, A:fox-beast-young, A:fox-storm-young, A:fox-nightcrawler-young, A:fox-magneto-erik and A:fox-jean-grey-young (+twin).
options: Keep as is (brief custody, released in the same scene)
Add a captor stage plus a return stage at Dark Phoenix for each
owner_calls.evidence: Each revised-timeline page says they were 'rendered unconscious by the U.S. military, who place mutant ability dispersing collars' on them and put them on a train to a containment facility.

owner_calls.question: In Days of Future Past (1973), Xavier's school is closed and has no students, and it is working again by Apocalypse. Should the X-Men stage break at Days of Future Past (Independent, then The X-Men again from X-Men: Apocalypse)? The same question applies to A:fox-beast-young, who stays with Charles at the closed school.
options: Add ['Independent','X-Men: Days of Future Past'] and ['The X-Men','X-Men: Apocalypse']
owner_calls.evidence: The record's own DOFP step reads 'with his school closed'. The wiki shows the school 'fully working' in 1983.

owner_calls.question: At the end of The Last Stand, Hank resigns from the cabinet, then is introduced as the new U.S. ambassador to the United Nations. Should that be a new stage after The X-Men?
options: Add ['United Nations','X-Men: The Last Stand'] before ['The X-Men','X-Men: Days of Future Past']
owner_calls.evidence: The wiki lists United Nations among his affiliations. The president introduces 'our new ambassador to the United Nations... Dr. Hank McCoy'.

owner_calls.question: At the start of X-Men: Apocalypse, Kurt has been captured and is held at an East Berlin mutant fight club until Raven frees him, and he joins the X-Men later in the film. Should '(from the start)' become a captor stage plus ['The X-Men','X-Men: Apocalypse']?
options: Add a captor stage at X-Men: Apocalypse (group name to be chosen by the owner)
owner_calls.evidence: 'Kurt Wagner was working in a Munich circus as an acrobat until he was captured and taken to a Mutant fight club... Mystique... shuts off the power'.

owner_calls.question: In 1983 (X-Men: Apocalypse), Alex is back from the Army. He brings Scott to the school, goes with Charles to the CIA, and destroys Cerebro on Charles's order before he dies. Should he rejoin The X-Men at X-Men: Apocalypse, instead of ending in the U.S. Army?
owner_calls.evidence: The wiki says he 'reunites with Hank McCoy and Professor Xavier once again' and acts with them. Its infobox lists the X-Men only as a former group.

owner_calls.question: In The Wolverine, the Black Clan takes Logan down with poisoned arrows and straps him into the Silver Samurai's machine at the Yashida Research Center, and he breaks free in the same sequence. Is this capture a stage?
options: Keep as is (brief, freed in the same scene)
Add a captor stage and return to ['Independent','The Wolverine']
owner_calls.evidence: 'The Black Clan, who had protected the House of Yashida for 700 years, then took down Logan with poisoned arrows.'

owner_calls.question: At the end of Runaways season 2, the LAPD arrests Catherine. In S3 she confesses and dies in prison. Should the custody be a stage (for example Independent from Runaways S3), or does she stay in The Pride until she dies?
owner_calls.evidence: 'Catherine and Geoffrey were therefore arrested and taken into custody'. She then 'chose to confess to the killing of Davis' and is killed in her cell.

owner_calls.question: Ikaris has a stage in 'The Survivors' from Marvel Zombies, but in episode 1 he only fights Carol Danvers while Kamala's group stumbles in, and he never joins them. Is 'The Survivors' meant as a loose category (non-zombie survivor) or as Kamala's team? This is outside the two kinds this pass checks, so it is flagged only.
options: Drop The Survivors stage, leaving ['The Eternals','(from the start)']
owner_calls.evidence: The MCU wiki biography covers only his endless battle with zombie Carol, and its relationships list Kamala, Riri and Kate under Enemies. Wikipedia calls him one of the 'survivors' only in the general sense.
